articles.title: US diesel prices hit an all-time-high
articles.text:
Drivers in the US are paying more than ever for diesel at the pump as the US-Israel war with Iran continues to hit Americans' wallets.

In the US, diesel is mostly used by commercial vehicles, such as trucks, trains, boats, buses, farming vehicles and construction vehicles.

The average price for one gallon of diesel in the US has hit $5.85, compared to an average of $3.71 a year ago and above the previous high following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA).

Fuel prices have soared since the Iran conflict began at the end of February, reflecting the surge in wholesale oil prices.

In response to rising fuel costs, US President Donald Trump recently pledged to "substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans" through an oil deal with Venezuela.

In January, the former leader of Venezuela, Nicolás Maduro, was seized by US special forces following a raid authorised by President Trump.

The latest agreement, announced on Saturday, calls for the development of 17 strategic oil fields with a proven potential of 65 billion barrels, as well as "an investment of more than $100bn (£73.9bn) and more than $209bn in taxes" for Venezuela, according to Interim Venuzuela President Delcy Rodríguez.

The US government will retain 55% control of a joint venture with an "experienced private operator in Venezuela", a US official told the BBC's US partner CBS News.

But some analysts have reacted with scepticism, including questioning whether the deal would address long-running obstacles that have deterred investment in Venezuela's oil industry.

Oil is a key ingredient in car fuel and supplies have been limited by Iran responding to the war by effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway south of the country through which a fifth of the world's oil is transported.

Rocketing pump prices have angered US voters ahead of the crucial midterm elections in November.

According to recent Reuters/Ipsos polling, Trump's approval rating has fallen to 33%, ​with just 31% of Americans approving of the conflict.

However, not all Americans face the same level of price rises. According to the AAA's data, those in the Western states pay much more than those elsewhere, due to tax differences and distance from US oil producers.

For example, in Washington, average diesel prices are $6.81 a gallon, compared to $5.03 a gallon a year ago.

As well as high diesel prices, Americans also face historically high petrol costs, with the average price per gallon reaching $4.15 compared to $3.20 a year ago.

articles.title: ‘There’s no plan’: as instability in global bond markets rises, what are the knock-on effects?
articles.text:
When Donald Trump was asked recently about the threat of rising interest rates on US government debt, he told baffled reporters: “The ultimate intervention is our military. And if we have to use that, we will.”

Perhaps not surprisingly, his bellicose words did not soothe fractious bond markets, and his resumption of the bombing campaign against Iran only made matters worse.

The past fortnight has seen a wave of instability sweeping through government bond markets in major economies – with knock-on effects for millions of borrowers. The interest rate, or yield, on 10-year US government borrowing hit 4.8% on Friday, up from 4.64% 10 days ago. At one point midweek, the 30-year yield touched its highest level since 2008.

Neil Shearing, the chief economist at the consultancy Capital Economics, said one impetus for the current wobble had been markets taking a fresh look at the state of US public finances. “There’s been a recalibration,” he said.

Total US government debt has surged past $40tn (£29.5tn), and annual deficits are forecast to be an eye-watering 6% of GDP for the foreseeable future.

Such figures were long deemed barely to matter given the status of US government bonds, or treasuries, as the ultimate safe-haven investment. But as the events that led up to the 2008 financial crisis revealed, things don’t matter in the markets until they do.

“I think we are starting to see a more realistic reassessment of the fiscal pressure in the US,” Shearing said. “What marks the US out is that there’s not really an acknowledgment of the fact that there might be a problem. There’s no plan.”

Russell Jones, a veteran bond market analyst at Llewellyn Consulting, said: “The thing about economics is that often markets delay the judgment and, you know, you can’t really time when they suddenly decide that that’s enough.”

The US treasury secretary Scott Bessent’s recent fumbled attempts to intervene in financial markets – to help Tokyo prop up the yen and then to calm bond yields – have only added to the sense that policymakers are panicking.

Layered on top of these concerns is a more immediate worry about inflation taking off again as a result of renewed hostilities in the Middle East. Oil prices have risen back above $90 a barrel since the US and Iran resumed tit-for-tat attacks.

That has increased expectations that central banks will have to raise interest rates – another factor that puts upward pressure on yields.

Every pronouncement by policymakers is being closely scrutinised for clues, including a key speech by the new Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh, last Friday that was read by markets as signalling a willingness to act.

The European Central Bank is expected to lead the charge with a rate rise next week, but markets are telegraphing higher borrowing costs across major economies.

That includes the UK, where investors are now pencilling in three quarter-point rate rises over the next 12 months, and Japan, where the decades-long period of deflation and rock-bottom rates is finally coming to an end.

A dramatic expansion of borrowing by AI “hyperscalers” in the US, to help fund the massive planned expansion of datacentres, has offered investors an alternative home for their cash – and raised questions about the market’s ability to absorb so much debt simultaneously.

Recent calculations by the investment group Vanguard put the value of debt issued by five major tech companies at $135bn (£100bn) this year, up from an average of $35bn between 2020 and 2024.

There is potentially an even more fundamental explanation for an upward shift in borrowing costs, too – based on the growing prevalence of inflationary shocks not just as a result of geopolitical chaos but because of the climate emergency.

Some economists, including the Bank of England policymaker Swati Dhingra, have argued these increasingly regular shocks, as a result of extreme weather events and resulting economic upheaval, could lead to structurally higher interest rates.

Whatever the causes of rising bond yields, the impact is already rippling out worldwide. Public borrowing has increased dramatically in recent years as policymakers have stepped in to cushion consumers against Covid shutdowns, wrestled with sharply higher energy prices since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and stepped up defence spending. That means small changes in global interest rates can have an outsized impact on government budgets.

In the UK, where £1 in every £12 of public spending already goes on debt interest, Andy Burnham, the prime minister, was pressed this week by the opposition leader, Kemi Badenoch, about the rising cost of government borrowing.

Higher yields on gilts, as UK government bonds are known, will feed through into predictions of higher interest rate costs for the Treasury ahead of the new chancellor John Healey’s autumn budget.

David Aikman, the director of the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, urged the government to take the opportunity to implement spending cuts and/or tax increases to help insulate the UK from higher borrowing costs.

“There will be a lot of talk about the fiscal rules. I think that’s slightly missing the point,” he said. “The big point here is we’ve just got a lot of debt, whether you’re missing the rules or not. And it means we’re really vulnerable.”

On the other side of the world, Australian policymakers have been wrestling with similar challenges. Bond yields have breached 15-year highs just days after the country passed A$1tn in government debt.

The timing of the two milestones comes at a difficult time for a Labor government that is under pressure to rein in historically high levels of spending.

Falling house prices in a property-obsessed nation are adding to a mood of discontent. Bets have firmed that the Reserve Bank of Australia could deliver another interest rate hike later this month to tame stubbornly high inflation.

Jim Chalmers, the treasurer, has been at pains to highlight Australia’s relatively strong budget position internationally. Australia’s debt is equivalent to about half the size of the economy, which pales against other advanced nations. Similarly, the commonwealth is running deficits, but of less than 1% of GDP.

Chris Richardson, an independent budget expert, said Australia’s government indebtedness wasn’t “bad by world standards”. “But it’s still a lot of debt. And the higher cost of money means the difficult choices that were there already are that much harder.”

For developing countries, these issues are all the more urgent. The International Monetary Fund warned earlier this year that these economies had become more exposed to the risk of higher interest rates, because of the growing importance of lending from short-term investors such as hedge funds, which tend to be more flighty during periods of market volatility.

Matthew Martin, of the advocacy group Development Finance International, said: “A lot of these countries are very near the edge, and if they have to go back to the markets and refinance another bond at 1% or 2% higher than it was before, that will mean even less money to spend on climate action, health and education.”

If higher yields are sustained, the effects will be felt far beyond the world’s treasuries, muddying the maths for corporate investments and putting upward pressure on mortgage rates, which in the UK have already started to rise.

Aikman argued corporate balance sheets worldwide looked less shaky than before the global financial crisis. “We’re not in the place we were in the run-up to 2008,” he said. But he pointed to “pockets” of concern, including the huge scale of debt-fuelled private equity projects that could prove vulnerable in a world of higher rates.

By the end of the week, the sell-off sweeping global bond markets appeared to have eased, for now. But it left yields at levels significantly higher than three months ago – and delivered a painful reminder to policymakers, including Burnham, that in globalised financial markets their plans can be buffeted by forces far beyond their control.

articles.title: Maria Bartiromo’s lawyer denies she was fired from Fox News anchor role
articles.text:
Maria Bartiromo’s lawyer sharply denied that she was fired from her job at Fox News on Friday, after reports that she was dismissed after divulging the network’s editorial guidance to the White House.

Fox announced Bartiromo’s departure on Thursday but provided no explanation, saying only in a statement that it was effective immediately.

“Effective today, Maria Bartiromo is no longer with FOX News Media,” the network said in a press release, adding in a statement: “We thank Maria for her work over the last 12 and a half years and wish her all the best on her next chapter.”

She had been with Fox for more than 12 years and hosted a popular three-hour weekday morning show for the Fox Business network, as well as a Sunday morning show.

Status News reported on Thursday that Fox instructed senior employees to avoid covering Donald Trump’s July primetime address, where he shared unproven and false claims about the 2020 election. Bartiromo, an avid Trump supporter, shared that message with the White House, according to Status News, a violation of company policy. Bartiromo was taken off the air shortly after.

In a statement, Bryan Freedman, Bartiromo’s attorney, called her, “one of the hardest-working journalists throughout her award-winning career” and denied the claims reported by Status News. Freedman has previously defended several journalists fired from their networks, including Don Lemon at CNN, Megyn Kelly at NBC News and Tucker Carlson at Fox.

“The irresponsible reports that have been published stating that Maria Bartiromo was fired or is no longer an employee of Fox are absolutely and unequivocally false,” Freedman said in a statement. “Make no mistake, we have the receipts and witnesses and they will come out whether through the courthouse or otherwise. Those reporting her firing or the incredulous facts supporting that fiction have exhibited a complete and utter reckless disregard for the truth.”

A Fox spokesperson pointed to the company’s original statement and said: “The release speaks for itself.”

Several former Fox News employees are now working at the Trump administration, including Trump’s defense secretary, Pete Hegseth. With the recent announcement that Trump’s press secretary, Karoline Leavitt, would be stepping down at the end of August, some have speculated that Bartiromo might be tapped to step into the role.

articles.title: US added 162,000 jobs in August, with unemployment rate holding steady
articles.text:
The US economy added 162,000 jobs in August, an uptick after a sluggish summer for the labor market.

The unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, still down from its most recent peak of 4.5% last November, according to new data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). Despite the relative stability of the unemployment rate, the number of new jobs added to the economy has been fluctuating, going from 214,000 in March down to a 21,000 gain in July and then back up in August.

Figures for job growth in June and July were both revised up. After revisions, job growth in June was 31,000 jobs, up from an initial 20,000, and July was revised up by 44,000 jobs, from an initially reported loss of 23,000 to a gain of 21,000.

Economists had predicted gains would be at least 50,000 new jobs. Earlier in the week, the payroll firm ADP reported private companies added 38,000 jobs in August, lower than initial expectations and the lowest month for new jobs since January. Meanwhile, outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas reported that layoffs have been going down and are 41% lower than cuts that were announced by this time last year.

Economists have pointed out that the labor market appears to be stalled in a “slow hire, slow fire” state, with neither growth nor contractions in jobs.

A separate BLS report from earlier this week showed job openings and layoffs had changed little in July. The number of people quitting their jobs also remained flat, suggesting workers are feeling less confident about their ability to find another job.

For many Americans feeling frustrated about the economy, a lackluster job market feels especially painful when paired with rising prices. US inflation has increased significantly since the start of the war with Iran, with the annual inflation rate going from 2.4% in February to 3.4% in July. In May, price increases reached 4.2%, the highest rate since 2023.

In recent weeks, persistent inflation has started to have a domino effect in the US economy after a sell-off in the US bond market. Yields for US Treasury bonds have been going up since the start of the Iran war, suggesting that investors are concerned about the long-term health of the economy. Higher yields could push up the price of loans, including mortgages, car loans and the interest rate on student debt, making things even more costly for Americans.

Economists are expecting at least one interest rate hike from the US Federal Reserve before the end of the year. Higher interest rates could help lower inflation, but at the risk of destabilizing the labor market.

Last week, Kevin Warsh, the Fed chair, gave his debut speech at the Fed’s symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, where he said the Fed was still committed to getting inflation down to its 2% target rate, but held off on making any firm suggestions on the central bank’s next move.

“We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed,” he said. “Otherwise, we have work to do.”

Donald Trump on Friday celebrated the new job figures and threatened to “stop trading with countries with which we have a deficit” if the Fed doesn’t lower interest rates.

“A STRONG COUNTRY MEANS A LOWER INTEREST RATE –IT’S A BETTER CREDIT… Very simple!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “We should have the LOWEST RATE of any country in the World, like ‘the old days’.”

articles.title: Nvidia to buy developer platform Hugging Face in $12.9bn deal
articles.text:
Nvidia will buy the popular developer platform Hugging Face for nearly $13bn, betting that support for ⁠open AI models could offset a potential slowdown in demand for the semiconductor giant’s chips.

Shares ⁠in Nvidia were ⁠slightly lower ​after the $12.93bn (£9.57bn) deal – which ranks among its biggest ever – was announced for the database of AI models on Thursday.

Hugging Face, based in New York and backed by the likes of Intel, Advanced Micro Devices and Amazon, was founded in 2016 by the French entrepreneurs Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf.

Nvidia is already a major open AI player in the US with ⁠its widely used Nemotron model and vocal support for the technology.

Acquiring Hugging Face will give it direct access to a platform developers use to ⁠collaborate and test and share tools, potentially providing insight and data that could help it narrow the ​technology gap with top American and ‌Chinese labs.

“Nvidia gains visibility into customer’s preferences and the AI models they use,” said Naveen Chhabra, principal analyst at Forrester. “They can see which models are trending, what datasets customers are downloading, and the architectures that are gaining traction weeks before they hit mainstream tech news.”

Demand for open-weight models ‌has surged from businesses balking at the steep bill of deploying generative AI. Chinese companies ‌such as DeepSeek, Moonshot and Z.ai have emerged as crucial players with models that can match the best from the US in tasks including generating computer code at a lower cost.

There are fears that some US firms could become reliant on Beijing’s models even as both countries race to dominate a technology they see as crucial to their future. The Trump administration has scrambled to respond to the wave of open models from China, weighing whether to restrict their use while also worrying about stifling American businesses that have taken to using them.

Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, was a signatory of an open letter earlier this year from major tech firms that advocated for open models and warned against government regulation that would stifle their use. Huang pledged that Nvidia would keep Hugging Face open after acquiring it.

“Hugging ‌Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem,” said Huang, adding that his company’s chips would not be required to ​build on or deploy through Hugging Face.

Under the deal, Nvidia will pay about $11.9bn to Hugging Face investors, while offering an equity-based retention program of up to $1bn for employees who join Nvidia.

For Nvidia, building up its open source business may help it cushion a demand slowdown from customers such as ⁠Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft, which are developing their own AI chips to cut reliance ​on its costly and ​supply-constrained processors. Several Chinese chip-making firms have also made recent advancements that could further disrupt the balance of power within big tech, though they face strict international export controls.

It has been a volatile year in the market for chipmakers, with a chip stock selloff in July wiping $1tn from the market caps of leading firms. Nvidia shares bounced back in August, though, with a strong revenue forecast leading to the second-biggest one-day gain in market history – adding $442bn to the company’s market value.

articles.title: Dutch central bank moves 86 tonnes of gold to UK from US and Canada, citing ‘geopolitical unrest’
articles.text:
The Dutch central bank says it has moved 86 tonnes of its gold reserves out of the US and Canada to London, citing “increasing geopolitical unrest”.

De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) said gold reserves held in London could be traded more easily than those held in New York and Ottawa.

“This makes it the quickest for DNB to deploy in a crisis situation,” the bank said in a statement on Wednesday.

“With this step, we have improved the deployability of the gold reserves. We assume that we will never need to deploy the gold, but it is nevertheless necessary to strengthen our resilience and preparedness,” said DNB’s president, Olaf Sleijpen.

The total Dutch gold stock amounted to 612.4 tonnes and was valued at €72.2bn ($83.7bn) at the end of 2025, said the DNB.

Before the deployment, the Dutch bank held 31.3% of its gold in New York and 19.7% in Ottawa.

After the move, each country accounted for 18.5% of the Dutch gold reserve.

The share of gold held in London increased from 18.1% to 32.1%. The bank still holds 30.8% of its gold in the Netherlands.

The transfer was carried out partially by buying and selling and partly by physically transferring gold, the bank said.

The bank moved more than 27 tonnes of physical gold from the US and Canada to Zeist.

The same quantity of gold was moved from Zeist to London, preventing the melting down of gold bars.

“By combining buying and selling and physical transport, the risks associated with physically moving a large quantity of gold have been spread,” the DNB said.

The operation took place between March and August of this year, it said.

Laurent Schwartz, president of the Paris-based National Gold Counter, which facilitates gold trading in France, said central banks had been moving their reserves around for about a decade.

“The current political context in the United States might also push certain central banks into favouring other storage locations,” he said.

The London market was the deepest and most liquid, Schwartz said, making it easier to deploy in times of crisis.

“Central banks can more easily lend their gold there to other banking institutions.”

John Plassard, an analyst at Cite Gestion Private Bank, said the Dutch move was intended “for there to be more immediate availability in the event of a crisis”.

For the moment, it was a “fairly one-off move”, but he warned that if other central banks followed suit, it could damage confidence in the US.

At the beginning of the year, there were concerns raised in Germany about the security of its central bank’s reserves in New York.

However, the powerful Bundesbank has decided for the moment not to shift its reserves away from New York.

“The New York Fed is and remains an important storage site for our gold,” the bank told public TV station ARD in January.

articles.title: Thieves steal more than 70,000 pints’ worth of Guinness from depot in Cheshire
articles.text:
The famous tagline “Guinness is good for you” applies only when the drink is bought and paid for, police have said, after thieves made off with more than 70,000 pints’ worth in Cheshire.

Officers said they believed two lorries were driven into a depot in Runcorn on Monday and attached to waiting trailers holding a combined total of about 800 barrels before being driven away.

Cheshire police said they hoped for a full recovery of the stolen barrels, and had appealed for witnesses who may have seen a lorry entering the Aston Lane area at about 7.45pm.

The first lorry was said to have connected to the HGV trailer before leaving the depot at about 7.55pm in the direction of the Mersey Gateway bridge. The second lorry arrived at the same site at 9.12pm and connected to another trailer before leaving at 9.30pm in the direction of Rainhill and Watkinson Way, police said.

DS McClatchy said: “It is famously said that ‘Guinness is good for you’, but that is only the case when it has been bought and paid for.

“It is with this in mind that we have wasted no time in launching inquires to identify those responsible for the theft of £115,000 worth of Guinness and the two trailers that housed the barrels. We will settle for nothing less than the full recovery of all the items stolen.”

When including the value of the trailers, the total value of the items stolen is estimated at about £205,000.

McClatchey asked anyone with information to speak to officers. “We would also ask any motorists who were driving in the area at the time of either of the incidents to please review any dashcam footage to see if you have captured anything that could aid our investigation.”

The stolen barrels, containing about 70,400 pints of Guinness, had been intended for delivery to pubs. Diageo, which owns the brand, has a packaging warehouse on the Whitehouse industrial estate on Aston Lane.

Police believe both HGVs were driven by men. The first driver was described as white with a short dark beard, and wearing a beanie hat. The second was believed to have been wearing a cap.

The trailers were described as white tri-axle curtain-side trailers with branding for the logistics company GXO on the curtains and rear doors. The trucks have the unique ID numbers DL736 and DL542 on the top left corner of their rear doors.

articles.title: Jamie Vardy: Burnley sign former England and Leicester striker
articles.text:
Former Leicester City and England striker Jamie Vardy has joined Burnley until the end of the season.

The 39-year-old, who is Leicester's record Premier League scorer with 145 goals, departed for Cremonese in 2025.

Vardy left the Italian side in the summer and now joins the winless Clarets who are bottom of the Championship.

"This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town," Vardy told the club website., external

"I can't wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction."

Vardy, who won 26 caps for England, scoring seven goals, spent 13 years at Leicester after signing from non-league Fleetwood Town in 2012.

He went on to score 200 goals in all competitions in 500 appearances.

Burnley, relegated from the Premier League last season, have made a poor start back in the second tier and have not won in five matches under new boss Nicky Hayen.

On Saturday they conceded two goals in the final 10 minutes to lose 2-1 at home to Bristol City.

"His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign," Hayen added.

"Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt."

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa president will stand for re-election in March
articles.text:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election in March, says football's world governing body.

Infantino, who has filled the role since 2016, has been under pressure following his scrapped plan to sell stakes in Fifa competitions to private investment firms.

Infantino's lucrative plan sparked a global outcry, with European football's governing body Uefa threatening to boycott all Fifa competitions, including the World Cup.

"The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027," read a Fifa statement.

"Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election."

Infantino refused to answer questions about his future when asked by reporters at the Women's Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday.

It is the first time Fifa has said he will run for a new term since the plan was announced following the summer's World Cup.

Should the 56-year-old Swiss be re-elected, he will serve until 2031.

Fifa this week accused Uefa of a "smear campaign against it and its leadership", in a challenge to litigation over Infantino's plan.

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Irish icon sails into retirement with the most perfect farewell
articles.text:
"There's nothing like an Irish family."

Katie Taylor addressed the Croke Park crowd as she paid tribute to her mother Bridget, but her extended family of 83,000 inside Croke Park and many more tuning in will have known this one was for them too.

Fairytale endings in boxing are a rarity, but Taylor is no ordinary fighter and her swansong proved as extraordinary as the fighter and person.

After 30 years lacing up the gloves, Taylor, 40, sails off into the sunset after the most perfect of farewells in front of her adoring fans at Dublin's iconic Croke Park, just three miles from the scene of her first official bout 25 years earlier.

The final act in the ring was to sweep past Flora Pili to cement her legacy in Ireland and beyond, bowing out as a three-time and two-weight undisputed champion.

It was a night of celebration, cheers and plenty of tears as fans and peers turned out for her victory lap, showing love and appreciation for a career which thrilled and inspired in equal measure.

"It was everything I expected and more," Taylor said at her final post-fight news conference.

"Thankfully I was able to hold my emotions together tonight as I was getting emotional all week and the last few months' preparation was so emotional.

"The atmosphere was so special. It was beyond my wildest dreams - what a special night."

Before her hand could be raised in the ring, there were battles to be won outside of it.

Born in 1986 as the youngest of four children to former Irish champion father Peter and mother Bridget - one of Ireland's first female officials - the very notion of women's boxing in Ireland appeared fanciful.

While older brothers Lee and Peter were welcomed into the boxing fold, Katie became K from Bray - a girl hiding her identity to simply compete in an exclusively male environment.

The fighting spirit and determination which characterises her sporting prowess is as much a feature of her personality, and in 2001 as a 15-year-old she took part in the first sanctioned women's bout in Ireland since it was outlawed following future world champion Deirdre Gogarty's 1991 debut in Limerick.

Perhaps fitting, as five years earlier, Taylor wrote to role model Gogarty, expressing frustration at the lack of opportunities to compete and outlining her dreams of one day being allowed to compete at the Olympic Games.

Prophetic words, as it was her exceptional talent on display in front of International Olympic Committee members in 2007 which convinced them to add women's boxing to the programme for London 2012.

All eyes were on her as Katie mania grew throughout the Games - her victory over Sofya Ochigava in the lightweight final a moment of national sporting joy comparable to the heady days of Jack Charlton's Republic of Ireland teams at the 1990 and 1994 World Cups - the Excel arena transformed into a small corner of Ireland on an unforgettable day.

A recognised star in Irish boxing circles was now a household name, her humble and gracious manner winning the hearts of a nation that has remained firmly in her corner.

"The 'ole ole oles' carried me all over the world: to Leeds, to Manchester, Brooklyn, Boston, Dallas, Manhattan," she reflected.

"This night is so special because I wanted to put on a performance for them. I don't think it was a career-best performance, but I got the win for them, just to say 'thank you'."

While her trophy cabinet is overflowing with gold medals and world title belts, perhaps her greatest legacy is leaving women's boxing in a vastly better place than she found it - that Serrano trilogy lifting women's boxing to new heights.

Taylor broke through the barriers with a grace which belied the obstacles she faced yet her quiet determination and humble nature will serve as an example of what can be achieved by belief, hard work and a refusal to accept her lot as young girls can now walk the path she laid.

Fierce inside the ring yet unassuming outside of it - even factoring in an impulse-buy speedboat, since sold - superlatives such as trailblazer, icon and Ireland's greatest sportsperson are not hyperbolic, for Taylor's status as a legend is in no way cliched.

She has indicated she will remain in the sport, but for now, there is time to savour an extraordinary career, with her place among boxing's greats set in stone.

Irish boxing is going to be a lesser place.

"I'm retired now so I can eat what I want, but I'm just going to enjoy a nice celebration and look back on a dream ending to a dream career.

"We all have our ups and downs. I think people resonate with your vulnerabilities and your successes - saw me cope with the heartbreak of Rio, the Chantelle Cameron loss and personal difficulties.

"My story is the story of everyone in this room."

articles.title: Diamond League Final 2026: Amy Hunt 'not afraid of anyone' after second-placed 100m finish
articles.text:
Amy Hunt says she is "on the up" and "not afraid of anyone" after finishing second in the 100m at the Diamond League final in Brussels.

The 24-year-old Briton finished in 11.06 seconds, behind Jamaica's Tina Clayton who won in 10.93, just one day after a third-placed finish in the 200m.

Hunt's performance surpassed American Olympic silver medallist Sha'Carri Richardson, who came third in 11.07.

It continues Hunt's fine late season form after winning four gold medals at the European Championships in Birmingham last month.

"I am 24 and on the up and up and up. I am not afraid of the other girls," said Hunt.

"I have so much love and respect for them and they are absolute icons but I love the challenge of going head to head with them.

"It takes me back to younger days racing boys in the school playground."

Hunt is planning to compete in the 100m and 200m again at the inaugural Ultimate Championships event in Budapest, which begins on 11 September.

"To come away with two podiums is no mean feat, and I am the only athlete to double up in the sprints and I came away with a second and a third," added Hunt.

Fellow Briton Georgia Hunter Bell came fourth in the 1500m despite being among the pre-race favourites.

Hunter Bell has won three international titles this year, including the world indoor 1500m, Commonwealth Games 800m and European 1500m, but never looked like threatening the top three in Brussels.

Poland's Klaudia Kazimierska came first with a time of three minutes 54.05 seconds, with Kenya's Dorcus Ewoi second and Australia's Jessica Hull third.

Hunter Bell said her performance was a result of a "long hard season", with the 32-year-old having competed in 19 races this year.

"I have done three championships so I am starting to feel it in my body," said Hunter Bell.

"I am struggling a little bit, even mentally to get my adrenaline up again week in, week out, but I am really lucky to be racing and to be happy and healthy.

"I just have to regroup before the Ultimate Championships next week, but I have to be happy with my consistency this season."

Elsewhere, Switzerland's Audrey Werro won the women's 800m final but was pushed all the way by Dutch athlete Femke Broeders-Bol.

With British Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson missing through injury, Werro hung on during the final straight with Broeders-Bol at her heels.

Werro, who has set the third, fourth and fifth fastest 800m times in history this year, finished in 1:54.75, which was 0.06secs in front of Broeders-Bol.

Brazil's Alison dos Santos and America's Masai Russell, who set world records in the men's 400m hurdles and women's 100m hurdles last week respectively, repeated their victories in Brussels but could not better the times they set in Zurich.

articles.title: Eilish McColgan wins fourth London Big Half after five-month injury lay-off
articles.text:
Eilish McColgan claimed her fourth victory at the Big Half in London on Sunday after returning to action following five months out with a broken toe.

The 35-year-old Scot suffered the injury during the London Marathon in April, crossing the line in seventh place with blood seeping through her shoe, and was forced to pull out of July's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

But McColgan showed the benefit of a month of warm weather training, completing a comfortable victory over the 13.1-mile course back in the English capital.

"I haven't even run 13 miles in training! I have mentally ticked that box and can push on from here, which is great," said the British women's half-marathon record holder.

She beat last year's winner Jessica Warner-Judd by one minute 19 seconds, finishing in a time of 1hr 10mins 54secs.

It was more than three minutes outside her best time for the course and well outside her British record for the distance of 1:05:43.

But McColgan added: "I came into this race in a different place from previous years, coming back into training for the last four weeks, so fitness was always going to be my biggest concern.

"I had fear over the broken toe, [so] I eased into it because of nerves and could really attack in the second half."

Britain's Jack Rowe missed out on a record fourth consecutive victory in the men's race, finishing in second place, 14 seconds behind Birchfield Harriers' Kadar Omar Abdullahi, who won in a time of 1:01:51.

Britain's David Weir defended his title in the men's wheelchair event, winning the race for the fifth time in its nine-year history in a new record time.

The 47-year-old, who retired from Paralympic competition in 2024, knocked 45 seconds off his own record for the course, which he set last year, winning in 46:13.

Eden Rainbow Cooper won the women's event in 52:47 to defend her title.

articles.title: Portsmouth fan clash: Police investigating Bielik incident at Fratton Park
articles.text:
Police are investigating an incident between Cardiff defender Krystian Bielik and home supporters during Portsmouth's 2-0 Championship win on Saturday.

Bielik was involved in a physical altercation with a fan as he went to retrieve a ball from the crowd late in the second half.

Hampshire Police were notified of the incident during the match and launched an investigation immediately afterwards.

"We can confirm that we are investigating an incident in which a teenage boy was reportedly the victim of a common assault during the football match at Fratton Park. Our enquiries are ongoing," the police said.

Several Portsmouth supporters made gestures that indicated they believed the fan had been grabbed by the throat.

Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy claimed afterwards that Bielik "got slapped in the face", while clips circulating on social media appeared to show the Poland international grabbing a young fan around his upper body.

In the aftermath, another fan threw a ball at the head of Cardiff defender Perry Ng. Both supporters were ejected from the stadium.

After the game Portsmouth head coach John Mousinho apologised to Cardiff City's players.

Pompey added in a statement:, external "Portsmouth Football Club are aware of supporter concerns regarding the incident involving a young fan and an opposition player at yesterday's match at Fratton Park.

"As this remains a safeguarding matter and is currently under investigation by both the club and the police, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further on the circumstances at this time.

"However, we are aware that a number of claims and assertions are circulating on social media. We would urge caution against speculation while enquiries are ongoing.

"The welfare and safeguarding of young people are of paramount importance to Portsmouth Football Club. We will continue to liaise with the relevant parties as enquiries progress.

"No further comment will be made at this stage while investigations remain ongoing."

The Football Association is aware of the matter and will review the details in the referee's match report before deciding whether any action should be taken.

Cardiff City said: "We are satisfied with the way that match officials dealt with the situation during the game, having been in full view of it. Player protection will always be of paramount importance to us."

articles.title: Arsenal transfer news: Gunners had more than 20 players on summer shortlist
articles.text:
Going into the summer transfer window as Premier League champions, hope sprang eternal for Arsenal.

An opportunity to capitalise, encouraged by a sense at Emirates Stadium that their competitors were in transition because of managerial instability.

If ever there was a moment to strike in recruitment, this was it.

The plans were ambitious: a shortlist with more than 20 players on it. They were targets at Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid, even at Chelsea and Tottenham.

But as the window shut on Tuesday night, you could not escape the sense of unfulfillment - certainly from a section of supporters.

Arsenal's close season was one characterised by some unquestionable successes, but also riddled by difficulties and frustration.

Ahead of their home match against Chelsea on Sunday, BBC Sport details Arsenal's transfer window and whether manager Mikel Arteta, sporting director Andrea Berta and, perhaps most pertinently, owners Kroenke Sports Entertainment can deem their summer operation a success.

Bruno Guimaraes's £75m capture from Newcastle United was Arsenal's most eye-catching signing.

Heading into the summer, Arsenal were keeping abreast of Guimaraes' situation at Newcastle, although others were considered a higher priority.

For instance, their interest in Elliot Anderson was widely reported, but it was clear the England international was joining Manchester City.

Guimaraes' former Newcastle team-mate Sandro Tonali and Bournemouth's Alex Scott were also among the midfielders explored before a move for the South American accelerated.

At the ages of 26 and 23 respectively, Tonali and Scott are younger than Guimaraes, who turns 29 in November.

But numerous factors, including availability and price - Tonali joined Spurs for a minimum £92m - made their signings difficult.

Aston Villa's Amadou Onana was also among the options considered, but the Belgium international suffered a serious knee injury at the World Cup.

By mid-June Guimaraes, who had universal backing inside the Emirates, emerged as the club's primary focus.

Berta knew the player's camp well and Guimaraes was admired by Arteta, who had made it clear he wanted proven talent to take his starting XI - rather than the wider squad - to greater heights.

Berta used his strong relationship with Guimaraes' representatives to facilitate Arsenal's move, hence why Newcastle maintained they had had no direct contact from the London club until days before his move was completed.

It is not uncommon for Berta to lean on intermediaries to conduct negotiations, although the approach has had varying degrees of success.

For instance, Arsenal actively sought moves for Leicester City teenagers Jeremy Monga and Louis Page over the summer.

But sources insist that the lack of club-to-club discussions meant both players ultimately did not join Arsenal, with Monga eventually signing for Manchester City when he appeared to be on the verge of moving to the Emirates.

That said, Berta's success in pivoting the club towards a deal for Guimaraes when it became clear other targets were not viable was well received behind the scenes at Arsenal.

The signing of Ezri Konsa was equally complex. Konsa was viewed internally as Arteta's first-choice defensive option.

Arteta wanted players used to the rigours of Premier League football - hence the moves for Guimaraes, Konsa and the failed efforts to land Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Konsa's ability to play at right-back was also viewed as a major benefit. Arsenal considered signing an orthodox right-back, with Ivan Fresneda among the options, but Konsa's versatility was a key factor.

But Berta appeared reluctant to meet Villa's valuation. A week before the Konsa deal was confirmed, Arsenal made a £40m offer, which was duly rejected.

Sources claim the deal was eventually sealed by the ownership at both clubs, and the transfer was agreed at £51m, with £4m in add-ons.

In the event of not reaching an agreement for Konsa, it is understood Tottenham duo Cristian Romero and Micky van der Ven were identified as targets – but Arsenal's north London rivals would not consider selling to them.

Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon is a player the club will continue to monitor, but clauses attached to his current contract make the deal difficult.

Tarik Muharemovic, who joined Leeds United, was another considered.

In attack, Christos Tzolis' impact since arriving from Club Brugge in a deal worth about £35m means the Greece international has been heralded as one of the discoveries of the summer.

It is understood the potential deal for the former Norwich winger was initially raised by an intermediary close to a senior member of the coaching staff during the close season.

Berta's number two, Maurizio Micheli, watched Tzolis play for his country against Sweden in June and was suitably impressed.

So far, the 24-year-old looks a positive addition to Arteta's squad.

Arsenal, who also made Piero Hincapie's loan deal permanent and signed Illan Meslier on a free transfer, are happy with the signings they have made.

The captures of Guimaraes and Konsa, who will both be 30 by the end of next season, have raised eyebrows given the combined £126m fee, amid concerns over how the pair's longevity may impact the natural evolution of the squad.

Yet it is undeniable that Guimares and Konsa add elite quality and experience to Arsenal ranks, and ultimately the club feel they paid the going rate to get those deals over the line.

While the club delivered proven talent for Arteta in defence and midfield, Berta's remit of adding an elite attacker ended in disappointment.

Rogers was the club's primary target heading into the window, and the early indications were positive amid a strongly held view internally that the forward wanted to join.

At the start of the summer, it was Arsenal's understanding that Villa valued Rogers at £100m. Arsenal valued Rogers at £80m.

Berta, however, was confident of negotiating the price down to a level he and the club believed could get the deal done.

In the meantime, however, Berta explored alternatives - Bradley Barcola, Kenan Yildiz, Yan Diomande and Nico Paz were admired.

Anthony Gordon was a long-term target, but he had agreed before the World Cup to join Barcelona.

Yildiz and Paz will continue to be realistic targets moving forward. Eli Junior Kroupi is another the club will watch once he returns from injury for Bournemouth.

Anderson's move from Forest to City for £116m, however, altered the complexion of Villa's outlook on Rogers' future.

Villa increased their valuation to £120m and ultimately Chelsea ended up signing the attacker for £117m.

Arsenal, it is understood, were given the opportunity to match Chelsea's offer but refused, believing their £80m valuation was fair - but it does beg the question of whether Rogers would be a Gunners player now if Berta had acted sooner.

Ultimately, the failure to land Rogers arrived as the first of a series of blows to Berta in his efforts to deliver a top-class left-sided attacker for the team.

Arsenal genuinely believed they had a realistic chance of signing Vinicius Jr before he decided to sign a new contract at Real Madrid.

Berta and Arteta were all in on the Brazil icon. The club were prepared finance the deal too.

While the transfer would likely have cost a British record fee and been one of the most lucrative remuneration packages in Premier League history, the benefit to Arteta's team and the Brazil superstar's commercial value meant Arsenal were absolutely prepared to complete the deal.

Yet well-placed sources expressed to BBC Sport over the summer that Vinicius did not want to leave Real, while others feared Arsenal were being used to strengthen the attacker's efforts to secure a more lucrative contract at the Bernabeu.

Those concerns came to fruition as Vinicius signed a new long-term contract in Spain in another Arsenal disappointment.

There were similar reservations about Arsenal's well-documented pursuit of Julian Alvarez.

The Atletico Madrid forward showed very little indication that he was willing to join Arsenal; his preference to join Barcelona was one of the worst-kept secrets of the window.

But Atletico's point-blank refusal to sell to Barcelona was deemed reason enough by Berta and Arteta to persist with their interest in the hope of Alvarez changing his mind until the closing days of the window.

Alvarez, however, preferred to stay at Atletico, even though his relationship with the club is at an all-time low.

Did Arsenal waste their time with Vinicius and Alvarez? The answer varies depending on who you speak to.

When it became clear Alvarez was unlikely, Berta explored his options.

Intriguingly, Arsenal have admired Chelsea striker Joao Pedro, who was deemed not for sale over the summer, although there were concerns over how he would fit into Arteta's system.

It is claimed Berta relies significantly on his vast network of agent connections rather than acting on the club's existing scouting information when analysing the market.

For example, last summer, when all the scouting information pointed towards a move for Benjamin Sesko, Berta's arrival meant the club pivoted to Viktor Gyokeres, who is currently second-choice striker.

This summer the club's late dalliance with Lyon winger Malick Fofana provided a further example of Berta leaning on his agency connections after management agency Roc Nation offered Arsenal an opportunity to sign the Belgium international.

Berta's relationship with Roc Nation was particularly prevalent this summer given Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius and the sale of Gabriel Martinelli, who are both clients of the agency.

It remains to be seen how much of an impact Arsenal's failure to sign a recognised top-level attacker impacts their season, particularly in light of Martinelli and Leandro Trossard's departures.

Arsenal headed into the window with a clear remit of ensuring the club become more sustainable and adept at trading.

Part of that directive is to ensure the club remain compliant with domestic and European financial regulations.

Depending on who you talk to, the size of the potential deals for Vinicius or Alvarez would have raised doubts over Arsenal's ability to stay within the regulations.

Nevertheless, ensuring they maximised the benefits of player trading will become an increasing part of Arsenal's financial operation in the future.

There was already evidence of that through the sale of Martinelli, whose £60m exit to Al-Hilal was the club's record departure. Arsenal have also secured a sell-on clause in the deal.

The exits of Martinelli, Trossard, Gabriel Jesus, Christian Norgaard, Jakub Kiwior, Fabio Vieira and Karl Hein secured the club in the region of £114m.

Through intermediaries, a possible exit for Myles Lewis-Skelly was explored, with a fee of about £80m believed to have been mooted for the midfielder.

Manchester United, who were attracted to Lewis-Skelly's ability to play at left-back, were interested but ultimately deemed his valuation too high.

Of course, it is Berta's job to have a firm grasp on the level of interest in the club's players and their market value but, nevertheless, the thought of Lewis-Skelly's departure resulted in huge uproar from supporters.

As BBC Sport revealed last month, the Gunners resisted any temptation to sell Ethan Nwaneri on a permanent deal, the academy graduate landing a season-long loan deal to Borussia Dortmund that includes a January recall option if required.

The minimum £15m fee secured in Trossard's deal to Besiktas is also viewed as a good deal inside the Emirates given the Belgian turns 32 in December.

Having spent nearly £450m in 12 months, Berta's work in the market has helped the club deliver their first league title in 22 years.

Yet, despite the money splashed, there remain clear issues in the squad - certainly in attack.

The summer window has left many supporters questioning Berta's body of work at Arsenal.

And with the average age of the squad increasing following the captures of Konsa and Guimaraes, can the current options build a dynasty of success before the club need to spend heavily again on regenerating the team?

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Zheng Qinwen beats Madison Keys from match point down to reach fourth round
articles.text:
Zheng Qinwen described her US Open third-round comeback win over Madison Keys as a "very dramatic match" - but that is somewhat of an understatement.

The Olympic champion, who had to come through qualifying to reach the main draw, found herself 5-0 and match point down in the third set against Keys.

But Zheng held firm and reeled off seven games in a row to secure a remarkable 1-6 7-6 (7-3) 7-5 victory over the 22nd seed and crowd favourite.

Keys, who won the 2025 Australian Open, appeared to be cruising towards a commanding victory after wrapping up the opening set in just 23 minutes.

But Zheng, who is rebuilding her career after undergoing elbow surgery last year, rallied, clinching it on a tie-break before snatching victory from the jaws of defeat against the American.

Zheng threw herself to the floor in relief and reflected afterwards on a difficult 12 months in which she has questioned if she will rediscover her form.

"Finally, a bit of luck is on my side," the 23-year-old said.

"I am just telling myself ever give up. Somehow, little by little, it's just happened.

"Tennis sometimes feels like rollercoaster. You see many times people have a match point, but at the end we made a comeback."

The Chinese star is the first qualifier to reach the women's fourth round at the US Open since Britain's Emma Raducanu, who went on to win the 2021 title.

Three months ago, Zheng could not hold back her tears in a news conference after a first-round exit at the French Open.

It was her first Grand Slam since undergoing surgery in July 2025 to correct a chronic injury caused by small pieces of bone floating in the elbow.

The injury came after a breakthrough 2024 where she reached the Australian Open final, won Olympic gold and made the US Open quarter-finals.

She had also enjoyed a promising start to 2025 before injury struck, advancing to the last eight at Roland Garros and climbing to a career-high of fourth in the world rankings.

It was understandable, therefore, why Zheng found a first-round defeat in Paris this year difficult to take - even if it was to eventual runner-up Maja Chwalinska after nine months on the sidelines.

Her ranking dropped as low as 160 and she had to contest a Grand Slam qualifying event for the first time in four years.

"After coming back from injury I felt I lost the energy and I forgot how to compete," she said.

Zheng seems to have recaptured some of her best form, having been taken to three sets in four of her six matches in New York so far.

She did not meet criteria for a protected ranking - for which players can apply if they are out injured for at least six months - because she made an early comeback to play her home tournament in Beijing in October 2025.

That meant she had to come through qualifying - something she found difficult to accept.

"I was even crying after I won the third match to reach the main draw," Zheng said.

"The main draw is just the beginning where all the players start. That was my beginning before.

"I fight so hard just to start like everyone else. For me, that was really not easy."

Her composure was on display against Keys - especially at 5-4 0-15 down, when she was forced to stop her service motion after a baby started crying in the crowd.

"If it's adult, probably I will look at him very hard or start to speak, but it's just a baby," Zheng joked.

"I can't do anything, you know? It's just a baby."

Zheng went on to win the next four points to level the tie - and the rest was history.

articles.title: Taylor vs Pili: Boxing world pays tribute to 'one of the best to ever do it'
articles.text:
Some of the biggest names in women's boxing have paid tribute to Katie Taylor after the Irish great ended her career with victory over Flora Pili at Croke Park.

Unified lightweight champion Caroline Dubois called Taylor "one of the best to ever do it", while Claressa Shields said the 40-year-old deserved to "ride off into the sunset".

Taylor beat Pili on points in Dublin to become undisputed light-welterweight champion and retires with 26 wins from 27 professional contests, Olympic gold and three undisputed title triumphs across two divisions.

"Thank you so much for paving the way," Londoner Dubois wrote on X. "Wishing you happiness, success and joy for this next season."

Taylor was sharper throughout, repeatedly beating the Frenchwoman to the punch before finishing with one final burst of combinations as the crowd rose to its feet.

American Shields - the self-proclaimed Greatest Woman of All Time - added: "Congrats Katie. Now ride off into the sunset. You deserve it all."

Super-featherweight champion Alycia Baumgardner described Taylor as "a trailblazer who helped set the stage for all of us".

"What a legacy," she wrote. "It's been a privilege watching your journey from the beginning."

Taylor's farewell unfolded in front of more than 80,000 fans in Dublin, with Westlife performing before the main event and Croke Park providing a fitting backdrop to her final night.

Former world champion Carl Frampton said Taylor's relationship with the Irish public was unlike anything else in boxing.

"You can tell that she doesn't enjoy doing stuff in front of the media, but she still has this adulation from everybody," the Northern Irishman said.

"Katie Taylor is different, she's special and there will never be another one like her."

Former cruiserweight world champion Tony Bellew described the occasion as one of the most remarkable exits the sport had seen.

"I don't think in all of my years of watching this game, I have seen an exit as beautiful, amazing and fitting," he said.

"She has just retired as the greatest champion ever. I have never seen a fighter leave as an undisputed champion on their own terms."

articles.title: Nottingham Forest 0-0 Tottenham: Expensive but misfiring Spurs still need to improve
articles.text:
It has been more than half a century since Tottenham have gone this long without a league goal to start the season.

A City Ground stalemate at Nottingham Forest at least gets Roberto de Zerbi's side their first point of the season but not to the extent they would want.

It followed defeats to Brentford and Newcastle which means Spurs have failed to score in their opening three league games for the first time since 1974-75.

Spurs did not play badly - they were the better side - but after their huge summer transfer outlay more is needed and expected.

De Zerbi preached patience and he is right - 10 senior arrivals means his team is still to find an identity.

And they did leave Forest with a point, something they have failed to do for almost three years.

Indeed, the video assistant referee's call to rule out Neco Williams' bundled second-half effort ensured it was not a third-straight Premier League defeat for Spurs.

Yet they have now failed to score in three successive Premier League games for the first time since November 2021, and improvement is needed at misfiring Spurs.

Last March's 3-0 win for Forest at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium provided the platform for the visitors' survival bid while leaving Spurs floundering until the final day.

Since then Spurs have spent over £300m on new players - contributing to the record £3.49bn Premier League outlay this summer.

Sandro Tonali, Jon Paul Van Hecke, Savio and Omar Marmoush were the new signings who started on Saturday, with De Zerbi remaining calm after another blank.

"We bought very, very good players but you can't just build the team with the names like in Football Manager," he told Sky Sports.

"We are disappointed for the result but for the performance very happy. Considering we started to work together last Thursday for the first time, for the first day.

"We have to improve in every part of football, organisation with and without the ball. Even today I thought we defended very well.

"We have to work because I think we played very well with the ball, we found the solution. I think we can be much better in the final third."

De Zerbi bemoaned Tottenham's decision-making with Marmoush a culprit, blazing over in the second half with Andy Robertson on an overlap and Mohammed Kudus waiting for a far-post tap in.

The former Brighton boss could see the positives but needs his men to discover their composure.

"I think we played well, in the last third we have to improve, we have to take better decisions, maybe keep calmer when we are close to doing something important.

"The chance when Marmoush shot, we had Robertson overlapping. If we take the right decision and if we play with Robertson on the second post there is Kudus to score.

"I am very happy with the spirit, with the organisation, their style of play is very clear, long ball and second ball, even the second ball we won many duels. They are good players.

"Taking a point in this stadium is not so easy. We are not happy because we didn't win but this is the right spirit and the right way to move on in this moment."

A draw was Tottenham's eighth in the league this year, their most across a calendar year since 2020, and they failed to have a shot on target in a top-flight match for the first time since April 2022 against Brentford under Antonio Conte.

Spurs have had 38 shots in the league this season with an expected goals of 3.3 and former midfielder Danny Murphy agreed with De Zerbi over what the visitors lacked.

"When Spurs did get in really good areas, they just rushed it and shot when they maybe should've passed," he told BBC Sport.

"They made the wrong choice on pullbacks or crosses when they're getting in wide areas, taking men on one too many times when they've already got the space.

"They were just missing that little bit of calmness and composure that you expect from top quality players.

"It takes time for some players [to find chemistry]. You could argue that Marmoush and Savio know each other anyway and bright footballers quickly learn each other's runs and movements.

"From a midfielder to a forward perspective, you're not always sure what they're going to do. Whereas if you played with someone for a while, it comes more naturally. So those relationships will build."

Mykhailo Mudryk arrived on deadline day, on an initial loan from Chelsea, looking to revive his career following his four-year ban for testing positive for banned substance meldonium in 2024, something he denied knowingly ingesting.

The Ukraine international came off the bench, his first Premier League appearance since being a second-half substitute in a 1-1 draw against Arsenal in November 2024.

"He needs time and he needs work, we have in that position Mathys Tel - big potential - but also Tel takes too many wrong decisions," added De Zerbi.

"Two big players with potential."

It was part of a second-half shake-up with Savio and Destiny Udogie being withdrawn after an hour in a planned double substitution on medical advice.

De Zerbi added: "Before the game the plan for Savio and Udogie was around 60 minutes. I'm not happy but football is like this, Savio not in the best physical condition to play 90 mins, he's a crucial player for us.

"Destiny is another crucial player. Kudus and Robertson played well but to start one game like today is not so easy to come inside from the bench and adapt immediately.

"I'm not happy when we have the plan but it's not my business, the management of players after injuries."

articles.title: Everton 2-2 Manchester United: Premier League – live
articles.text:
So United concede twice for the third time out of three. And Everton remain unbeaten!

Updated at 10.58 EDT

FULL TIME! Everton 2-2 Man United

The whistle, and a roar: the draw is greeted like a win.

GOAL! Everton 2-2 Man United (Maitland-Niles 90+6)

And now they’ve done it again! Maitland-Niles announces himself with a screamer.

Updated at 10.59 EDT

90+5 min Corner for Everton! They equalised with one last weekend…

90+4 min Chance for Everton! More wiggling from Grealish, leading to a shot for Hackney, which goes over the bar.

90+3 min Another glimmer for United as Yoro gets well forward, but his little through ball is not what Sesko had ordered.

90+3 min Dorgu and Mazraoui combine to reach the box, but the move fizzles out. Rashford and Shaw they are not.

90+2 min George goes for goal, and glory, again – but he’s so excited that he has forgotten about the offside rule.

90+1 min Grealish goes for a big shot, blocked by Maguire. And now Shaw is going off, to be replaced by Mazraoui. Five mins of added time!

90 min Paul Moody was right: Luke Shaw has put in a performance to Silence the Doubters.

GOAL! Everton 1-2 Man United (Sesko 88)

He’s done it again! A neat pass from Fernandes, a classy cross from Shaw, a purposeful header from Sesko.

Updated at 10.54 EDT

86 min United’s last shot on tatget was 37 minutes ago – the one that went into the net.

84 min Credit to David Moyes, for bringing Hackney on, and for keeping George on – he switched to the right when Grealish arrived.

83 min United subs: Yoro for Dalot, Santos for Mainoo.

Updated at 10.44 EDT

GOAL! Everton 1-1 Man United (George 83)

And there it is! Hackney shimmies through the No 10 zone and slips the ball rightwards to George, who takes a touch and then blasts the ball past Lamnens.

Updated at 10.50 EDT

81 min The free kick finds Branthwaite, whose flicked header is on target and punched clear by Lammens. Everton still on top…

78 min The next yellow goes to Dalot, as Grealish sharpens his dance steps and has to be clawed back. Free kick to Everton on their left wing.

78 min Grealish shapes to dance past Dalot, who tackles him solidly. Fernandes goes down, some way away. Everton advance into the box, where Mainoo makes an even better tackle. Maguire gets booked, possibly for complaining about Fernandes.

“Luke Shaw,” says Paul Moody. “Answering recent criticism…l ively game… nervy at 57 min, must remember to breathe out.”

77 min Garner goes off to be replaced by another new recruit, Ainsley Maitland-Niles, three years after his last PL appearance fro Southampton.

76 min Garner goes down off the ball! David Moyes will hope it’s just cramp.

75 min A third Everton sub: Hayden Hackney, Michael Carrick’s mini-me, replaces Rohl, so Garner may be moving to right-back.

74 min United escape and Mbeumo tries to reprise his goal, only to run into yet another block.

73 min A sharp shot from Dewsbury-Hall, blocked by a combination of Barry and Martinez.

72 min Maguire tries a through ball to Sesko, who doesn’t see it coming. It feels as if United will need a second goal to get the win.

70 min Everton free kick: nothing doing except Tarkowski climbing all over Maguire, which is no mean feat.

69 min Subs for United: Sesko for Cunha, as expected, and Dorgu for Rashford, as not expected yet unless there’s a niggle involved.

68 min Grealish could have an assist already! He wiggles in from the left and tees up Dewsbury-Hall, whose shot is all accuracy and no power.

67 min It’s Grealish time! On comes the dear old ponytail, out comes the big smile, and out come the cheers.

Updated at 10.33 EDT

66 min The game has swung from too slow to not slow enough for anyone trying to capture it. In the past minute alone, we’ve had a shot from Tielemans with his left foot and Shaw with his right.

64 min Rashford twists and turns, leaving Rohl with twisted blood – and a yellow card. But the free kick is wasted as Fernandes blazes a follow-up shot into Row Z.

63 min Luke Shaw has been booked for something I missed, sorry. Meanwhile the commentators are full of praise for Tarkowski, who made that tackle on Cunha.

61 min Almost vintage Rashford! He runs and runs and then does some dancing before back-heeling to Cunha, who goes down – no pen, says John Brooks.

60 min The hourglass flips over, and Sesko and Grealish wonder when they will come on stage.

59 min Everton push forward with more conviction, roared on by the crowd. Barry has a shot smothered by Shaw, and then Dewsbury-Hall has more time but can’t get a clean connection.

58 min United again counter from the corner, with only slightly more success. Cunha delays his pass and picks the wrong runner – Mbeumo, who has George to race with, rather than Rashford in more space.

articles.title: Formula One 2026: Kimi Antonelli ends 60-year home wait at Italian GP after overtaking George Russell – live reaction
articles.text:
Surely that is the drive of the season! A performance befitting of a potential world champion.

This is the top 10 today:

Antonelli: “Yeeeeeeesssssssss! Oh my God! Yes! Woohoo!”

The Italian crowd, dressed in red, give a wild reception to the 20-year-old. What a talent.

Antonelli wins the Italian Grand Prix!

The first Italian to win his home grand prix since 1966! A remarkable victory, considering Antonelli started the day in 19th place! NINETEETH! Russell has to make do with second.

Lap 52: Norris and Piastri battling for fourth. The former veers onto the grass but Piastri holds on!

Lap 51: That is surely that. Russell ran out of road, and simply didn’t have the pace on his ancient hard tyres. He will be aggrieved that he didn’t make that pit-stop. A remarkable race for Antonelli, who now just needs to keep four wheels on the track to bring this home.

Antonelli takes the lead with three laps remaining!

Lap 50: Luckily for Antonelli, his trip to the gravel only cost him a couple of seconds, and over the course of Lap 49, the Italian is able to regain that ground. As the cars enter the home straight once more, Antonelli makes the overtake, correctly this time and we have a new race leader!

Antonelli onto the gravel!

Lap 49: Russell holds on into turn one! The Brit defends the inside and Antonelli wildly swings back out to the outside, loses grip and skids onto the gravel! Scenes! “What the fuck happened there?”, cries Antonelli over the radio.

Lap 48: Antonelli is now breathing down the neck of Russell! This is now surely a question of time.

Lap 47: Both Mercedes and Ferrari dropped the ball when they failed to bring in Russell and Hamilton during that virtual safety car. Why was Antonelli brought in for new tyres and Russell wasn’t?!

Lap 46: Antonelli has just set the fastest lap of the race. The 20-year-old is absolutely flying, while the damage on Russell’s hard tyres is now visible.

Mercedes’ radio: “We can see the damage on the tyre and these vibrations picking up every lap, so let’s take no risks. Bring it home.”

Which is code for: ‘If/when Antonelli passes you, don’t contest it too much and risk coming off the track’.

Not what Russell will want to hear.

Lap 45: Antonelli is now just three seconds behind Russell, who can now see his teammate in his rear-view mirror. Our race leader appears to be a sitting duck.

Lap 44: Just over three seconds separate Verstappen in third and Hamilton in seventh.

Lap 43: Ten laps to go, here’s where we are!

Lap 42: Verstappen locks up into turn one and is forced to take the run-off but expertly negotiates the turns and limits his damage to a couple of places.

Lap 41: Gasly is talking about the track degrading at turn two. Liam Lawson has also mentioned that section on his radio.

No further action taken on Russell regarding yellow flag infringement

Lap 40: That’s big for our race leader but Antonelli is still closing. The Italian is now just 5.7 seconds off the lead with 13 laps remaining.

Lap 39: A lot rests on that potential yellow flag infringement, but we are set for a brilliant end to this grand prix.

Russell: “Are the lap times good enough at the moment?”

Mercedes: ‘Currently, Kimi forecast to catch right at the end of the race.”

Lap 38: “Why on Earth didn’t they bring in Hamilton under the VSC? Were they taking a nap?” asks Beau Dure. It does seem odd. Hamilton was in the ascendancy but his race has been completely scuppered since that virtual safety car.

Russell noted for a yellow flag infringement!

Lap 37: Russell is officially under investigation for a yellow flag infringement. That means one of the stewards has seen something and could result in a five-second penalty. With Antonelli less than eight seconds behind Russell and 16 laps to go, that could be curtains for the Brit’s hope of victory.

Lap 36: How long will Russell and Piastri last on those hard tyres? Not long, it appears, as Antonelli rushes past the latter to take second!

Lap 35: Another boost for Antonelli with Hamilton forced into the the run-off area on turn one. The Ferrari driver is struggling for grip on his tyres and Antonelli has another easy pass up to third!

Lap 34: Just over 10 seconds now between Russell and Antonelli. This is very much on.

Lap 33: “If Russell loses this race, I think he should just forget about the championship,” emails Edwin Innih Imoesi.

I agree. This is approaching make or break for the Brit’s season.

Lap 32: Russell has a six-second lead over Piastri. One of Sky’s F1 boffins has estimated that if Antonelli can retain this speed, he will be in contention for the lead in around four laps.

Lap 31: So, here’s where we are on Lap 31. Antonelli and Verstappen are flying through the field, following their pit-stops.

Lap 30: Russell is still out on those hard tyres, can he last the whole race on that? That is the big question for the Brit, who now has a big lead over the rest of the track. ““I’ve got massive derating in this strat, are you sure this is good?” asks Russell regarding his tyres.

“Keep this strat,” replies the Mercedes engineer.

Yellow flag: virtual safety car deployed

Lap 28: Lance Stroll has come off the track, so everyone has had to come down to the same speed. This is a perfect time for a pit-stop and Antonelli pits! New medium tyres for Antonelli, who will now be lightning quick, even if he has fallen to sixth, around 15 seconds behind Russell. Verstappen also pits, it’s hard tyres for the Red Bull.

Lap 27: Antonelli is a couple of car lengths behind Russell, stalking his teammate.

Lap 26: Verstappen is still less than two seconds behind, so juuuuuuust outside of the overtake mode.

Lap 25: Mercedes will hope that their two drivers slingshot each other away from Verstappen and the rest of the racing track. But it doesn’t appear that Russell or Antonelli are listening.

Lap 24: More info from the Mercedes radio: “George had been given the message to build the gap to Verstappen. If he can’t do that then we will invert.”

Lap 23: “We have to stop yo-yoing, we just have to build that gap”, plead the Mercedes radio to their two drivers. Antonelli replies“Yeah right, and then he can pass me. Do you want me to sit behind or what?”

Russell retakes the lead!

Lap 22: This is going to happen all afternoon, isn’t it?! So long as the two Mercedes are battling for the lead in such close quarters, the lead will continue to change. The second-placed car is always going to have the advantage going into that mammoth straight, which is where all the overtakes are taking place. Russell roars past Antonelli once more. He leads.

Updated at 10.20 EDT

Lap 21: Norris is up to sixth, with Gasly falling again. Verstappen is third, Piastri fourth, Hamilton fifth, Norris sixth and Gasly seventh.

Lap 20: Both Antonelli and Russell swap turns in taking the lead but Antonelli finishing the 20th lap at the front. The two Mercedes cars now have clear distance to Verstappen, 1.4 seconds in front, so out of the overtaking zone to the Dutchman.

Lap 19: Russell tries to regain the lead, but Antonelli holds on! Interesting that the Italian was able to hold on, despite Russell having the overtaking mode and that extra half megajoule of power.

Antonelli takes the lead!

Lap 18: A huge roar from the home crowd as the Italian rounds his teammate Russell and takes the lead! It now appears to be a three-horse race as Antonelli–Russell–Verstappen slink around the track, a good distance from the rest of the pack.

Lap 17: What a race this is. Hamilton and Piastri are fighting for fourth place, with the Ferrari winning the battle.

Lap 16: Antonelli takes second from Verstappen! This is remarkable racing from the 20-year-old Italian. Verstappen is not happy. “The car is completely broken on its rear axle,” he tells Red Bull radio.

Russell regains the lead from Verstappen!

Lap 15: The Mercedes makes no mistake with his second attempt and Verstappen is forced to cede the lead!

Just 3.8 seconds separate the top seven here. Wooooosh.

Lap 14: Verstappen and Russell are having a right ding-dong battle at the front. Russell makes the move but fails to get a car length in front of Verstappen and the Dutchman is just able to cling onto the lead into the corner. EEeeeeeeesh.

Antonelli into the podium places!

Lap 13: Remarkable! Having started at the back of the grid, Antonelli is now just 1.5 seconds behind teammate Russell in second! Verstappen still leads.

Verstappen takes the lead!

Lap 12: Verstappen, on the medium tyres, carries huge speed going into that home straight, and the Dutchman takes the outside line, easily surpassing Russell – almost waving to the Brit – into that first corner. We have ourselves a new leader!

Lap 11: Gasly is falling like a stone through the field to sixth. The Alpine driver is helpless as Piastri and Antonelli take fourth and fifth respectively.

Lap 10: Hamilton up into third place! The Ferrari roars down the outside on that home straight and simply outstrips Gasly on the inside, and takes position for the second corner in that first chicane.

Lap 9: Things have settled somewhat after that breathless start. Hamilton has just recorded the fastest lap. The slipstreams are real at Monza. Gasly is struggling in third, the Alpine driver is already being told to manage his medium tyres! Hamilton licking his lips in fourth.

articles.title: Diana memorial fountain shut all summer by technical fault
articles.text:
The Diana Memorial Fountain in Hyde Park - which has long been a popular place to cool down in hot weather - has been kept dry all summer due to a technical fault.

Royal Parks, the charity that maintains the central London park, apologised to visitors who found it without water "particularly given the prolonged high temperatures we've been experiencing".

The fountain opened in 2004 in memory of Diana, Princess of Wales who died nearly seven years earlier.

The closure was initially triggered by a mechanical breakdown in the pump that draws water from the local borehole. The pump was fixed, but software used to control the system then failed, preventing the water supply from being restored.

The closure was publicly announced by Royal Parks on 1 July.

The charity's spokesperson acknowledged that the fountain had "remained dry for longer than we hoped" while specialist teams worked to resolve the software issue.
